toegepas.voor: Sy plan om mense te skei, het apartheid geheet
toegepas.na: Sy plan om mense te skei, is apartheid genoem
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Het ... geheet' is stiff and formal for Grade 4; 'is ... genoem' is the natural way to say what something was called.
toegepas.fout: 'het apartheid geheet' is stiff for a plan; 'heet' sits more naturally with names of people and places
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'is apartheid genoem' is the plain, natural way to say what the plan was called, with the same meaning and the protected word untouched.

toegepas.rede_vinder: The past participle belongs at the end of the clause; putting the prepositional phrase after it follows English word order.
toegepas.fout: the prepositional phrase follows the participle, in English word order
toegepas.rede_keurder: Standard Afrikaans puts 'met protes' before 'gehelp'; same people, same action, and 'ANC' is outside the change.

toegepas.blok: Hy het gekies om te vergewe
toegepas.voor: In 1990 is hy vrygelaat en baie mense
toegepas.na: In 1990 is hy vrygelaat, en baie mense
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: a comma before 'en' when it joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: missing AWS comma between two clauses with their own subject and verb
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'hy is vrygelaat' and 'baie mense het gedink' are two full clauses joined by 'en', so the AWS 2017 comma belongs there.

toegepas.blok: Hy het gekies om te vergewe
toegepas.voor: toegewyd en heelhartig verbind aan ander mense
toegepas.na: toegewyd en heelhartig aan ander mense verbind
toegepas.rede_vinder: Afrikaans puts the prepositional object before 'verbind'; the current order follows English 'committed to'.
toegepas.fout: 'verbind aan ander mense' follows English 'committed to' word order
toegepas.rede_keurder: Afrikaans puts the prepositional phrase before the participle at the end of the clause; the meaning is unchanged.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Opstaan vir' is a calque of 'stand up for'; the Afrikaans idiom is 'opkom vir'.
toegepas.fout: 'opstaan vir iemand' is a calque of English 'stand up for'
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Opkom vir iemand' is the Afrikaans idiom for defending someone; same action, same person.

laat_vaar.voor: werk tot voordeel van ander en nie van homself nie
laat_vaar.na: werk tot voordeel van ander en nie tot sy eie voordeel nie
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Tot voordeel ... nie van homself nie' is an incomplete parallel; the idiom needs 'tot sy eie voordeel'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The original is a clear, grammatical ellipsis ('nie [tot voordeel] van homself nie'); the proposal only makes it longer.

laat_vaar.blok: Gewone mense kan dit ook doen
laat_vaar.voor: Hulle stories behoort aan mense oral en nie net aan hulle eie lande nie
laat_vaar.na: Hulle stories behoort aan die hele wêreld en nie net aan hulle eie lande nie
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Aan mense oral' is awkward and does not parallel 'lande'; 'die hele wêreld' keeps the meaning and balances the contrast.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'aan mense oral' is natural Afrikaans and was written to a curriculum order for a value statement; 'aan die hele wêreld' can read as a claim of reach, so the meaning would move.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: After 'manier' a verb takes the 'om te' infinitive; 'manier van regeer' is colloquial.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'n manier van regeer' is an established Afrikaans construction (like 'manier van doen'), and the change to a glossary definition would put 'regeer' twice in quick succession.

na_skrywer.blok: Gewone mense kan dit ook doen
na_skrywer.voor: Hy het self gesê hy is nie 'n heilige nie en hy het aangehou probeer
na_skrywer.na: Hy het self gesê hy is nie 'n heilige nie, en hy het aangehou om te probeer
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: AWS comma between two clauses with their own subject and verb, which also shows that he kept trying rather than that he said so; 'aangehou om te probeer' is the standard construction.
na_skrywer.fout: it is unclear whether 'hy het aangehou probeer' is part of what Mandela said or the narrator's own statement
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The proposal says itself that the comma decides who says he kept trying, which turns two possible readings into one and settles a content question about his words, so the writer has to decide it; 'aangehou probeer' is acceptable Afrikaans as it stands.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

na_skrywer.blok: Gewone mense kan dit ook doen
na_skrywer.voor: Hierdie eienskappe pas ook in jou klas en jou huis
na_skrywer.na: Hierdie eienskappe kan jy ook in jou klas en by die huis gebruik
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: 'Pas in jou huis' reads as physically fitting into the house; 'by die huis' is the idiomatic preposition.
na_skrywer.fout: 'pas ook in ... jou huis' can read as physically fitting into the house
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The fault is real, but the proposal changes 'fit' to 'use' and makes the learner the subject, and 'eienskappe gebruik' is itself awkward, so the writer should find another fix.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

na_skrywer.rede_vinder: AWS: 'ná' with the accent when it means 'after', to separate it from 'na' (towards); the lesson itself writes 'Ná sy vrylating'.
na_skrywer.fout: the definition writes 'na' where the lesson body writes 'Ná', but the accent is optional where no confusion is possible
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: This is a consistency choice in a glossary definition, not a plain spelling error, so the writer should make it for every lesson that uses this definition.

vlae.blok: Hy het gekies om te vergewe
vlae.teks: Hy was toegewyd en heelhartig verbind aan ander mense.
vlae.rede: Besides the word order, 'verbind aan' (committed to) is itself close to an anglicism and the sentence reads wooden for Grade 4; 'toegewyd' and 'verbind' may be CAPS quality terms, so I have not replaced them. A person or the writer should decide whether a plainer sentence is allowed.
